skill.name: pr-to-video
skill.description: Creates HyperFrames explainer videos from GitHub pull requests using PR metadata, diffs, narration, captions, and rendered frame compositions.
skill.summary: Turn a GitHub pull request into a narrated code-change explainer video.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: AI review found real operational use of external commands, including gh, node, ffmpeg, and ffprobe, plus controlled network access for GitHub avatars and CDN assets. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, relative reference paths, RegExp.exec calls, parser regexes, or comments. No prompt injection text was found in the skill files, but PR body text should be treated as untrusted when used for planning.

remediation.issue: External command execution through GitHub CLI and media tools
remediation.suggestion: Document every required command, prefer read-only GitHub credentials, and show command failures instead of continuing with fabricated PR data.
Allow HF_MEDIA_ENGINE only when explicitly trusted, or restrict it to known project paths before executing node.

remediation.issue: Untrusted PR text is used as planning material
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to treat PR descriptions, comments, commits, and diffs as untrusted evidence, never as instructions.

remediation.issue: External CDN dependency in generated HTML
remediation.suggestion: Vendor GSAP locally or keep SRI pinned and document that preview or render may request jsDelivr.

content.value_statement: Pull request changes can be hard to explain to reviewers and stakeholders. This skill turns PR data into a narrated HyperFrames video workflow.
actual_capabilities: Fetches pull request metadata, file lists, comments, and diffs through the GitHub CLI.
Builds a bounded PR brief with contributors, changed files, and representative diff hunks.
Creates a Claude-style HyperFrames design system for code-change videos.
Guides storyboard, script, narration, captions, transitions, frame assembly, and MP4 rendering.
Downloads optional contributor avatars from GitHub for credits frames.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI access, and private repositories require authenticated GitHub credentials.
Requires HyperFrames, Node.js, and local media tooling such as ffmpeg for full rendering.
Best suited to pull requests, not website tours, product promos, or topic explainers.
Video quality depends on the PR description, diff clarity, and user approval at review gates.

use_cases.title: Review-Focused Change Summary
use_cases.description: Create a concise video that explains what changed, why it matters, and where reviewers should focus.

use_cases.title: Feature Reveal for Developers
use_cases.description: Turn a merged feature PR into a short technical video for release notes or community updates.

use_cases.title: Refactor Walkthrough
use_cases.description: Explain a complex refactor with selected diff hunks, mechanism diagrams, captions, and narration.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Small PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short PR explainer video for this pull request: <PR URL>. Use the default audience, length, and landscape format.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a feature-reveal video for <owner>/<repo>#<number>. Aim it at developers and highlight the user-facing behavior change.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Refactor Walkthrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactor walkthrough for this PR. Use three code beats, one mechanism diagram, and a calm technical narration style.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Release Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PR video for release review. Keep it under two minutes, include contributor credits, and ask before final render.

output_examples.input: A focused bug-fix pull request with a small diff and clear reproduction notes.
output: A 30 to 45 second narrated fix explainer.
Frames covering the problem, the changed code path, and the resolved behavior.
Captions, transitions, and a rendered MP4 after user approval.

output_examples.input: A large feature pull request with many changed files and several contributors.
output: A structured video plan that selects representative hunks instead of reading every file.
A feature reveal arc with code surfaces, mechanism visuals, and optional contributor credits.

output_examples.input: A refactor PR where the main value is easier maintenance and safer data flow.
output_examples.output: A developer-focused walkthrough that compares before and after behavior, then explains the engineering impact.

best_practices: Use a specific pull request URL or owner, repository, and number.
Approve the storyboard before audio and frame generation begin.
Review generated frames and captions before rendering the final MP4.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for a product promo without a pull request.
Do not ask it to invent PR details when GitHub access fails.
Do not run it with broad credentials when a read-only GitHub token is enough.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a GitHub pull request URL, an owner and repository reference, or the current checked-out PR.

faq.question: Does it capture a website?
faq.answer: No. It reads PR metadata and diffs, then creates synthetic HyperFrames video compositions.

faq.question: Can it work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, if the GitHub CLI is authenticated with access to the private repository.

faq.question: Does it require HeyGen sign-in?
faq.answer: HeyGen sign-in improves voice and music options. The workflow can continue offline with local engines when supported.

faq.question: What does the final output include?
faq.answer: The workflow produces an assembled HyperFrames project and a rendered MP4 after the user approves the review step.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
